My two pairs of pruning shears were sharpened in a flash. I had been trying to get them sharpened since last spring, when I took them to the OSH workbench. The handyman in charge couldn't unfreeze the screws to disassemble the secateurs for sharpening and advised me to buy replacement screws, which I did from Spring Valley (the Felco for $16). When at length I returned to OSH the sharpener was off work that day. I never managed to get to Truitt and White Lumber to order the left-handed screw for the Corona. At the Fix-It event Adam showed me how to use a bastard hard mill file to sharpen the (soft steel) secateurs while still assembled. One of the Felco blade made be slightly out of true and need pounding on a work bench. He also advised me to use a sharpening stone on hedge clippers (hard steel). After all that fuss with screws, purchasing the wrong sharpener tool, reading all kinds of instructions included with the shears and online, the deed was done in a moment. After sixty-three years of gardening I finally learned how to sharpen my own shears.. Purchase a bastard hard mill file; open the shears wide, follow the angle of the blade, filing in one direction away from your body. For safety brace the tool firmly on the edge of the table. Be careful not to cut yourself. That's it. Get a whetstone for the hedge clippers.
